This study investigates the transformation kinetics and mechanical
properties of high C and Al-containing nB-steels, with a focus on clari
fying the microscopic mechanisms that underlie these properties. Pre
cipitation kinetics simulations are used as a complementary tool in this
investigation. The novelty of this work lies in the systematic investiga
tion of transformation behavior and mechanical performance in nano
bainitic steels with relatively high C–Al contents, a compositional
range that remains insufficiently studied in the literature, given its
relevance for low-density, high-strength applications.
2. Materials and methods

minimize the density and bainitic transformation time (Bt) via Al, which

of the austenite single-phase region, and shifting it to higher tempera

4. Conclusion
This work systematically compares bainitic transformation kinetics
and tensile behavior across five low-density Al–C steels with varied C–Al
levels and Ti microalloying, supported by LOM, SEM /EDX, XRD, EBSD,
and MatCalc simulations. The conclusions are as follows.
1. Bainitic Transformation Kinetics: Steel S5 exhibited the fastest bai
nitic transformation ( Bt: 700–1000 s), whereas S3 (with the highest
Al content ≈8 wt.%) was the slowest (Bt: 14,000–43,000 s,
depending on austempering temperature). In S3, the presence of

showed initially rapid nucleation but was slowed by bainitic sheaf
impingement (Bt: 3000–3500 s). Notably, the transformation time
was not affected by a small Ni addition (0.78 wt.% in S4 and S5).
2. UTS-El (PSE) Performance: Despite compositional differences,
